agree.reason: The plain, respectful tone, the job guarantee and the attention to scheduling would keep some staff, but it never says why phone and chat work could suit people who chose branch work, so the long-tenured staff who don't want phones are given little reason to stay over a large severance.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the brief's unsupported claim that the change makes everyone's job better, but it invents commitments the brief never gave: one-on-ones with managers this week, schedules that take childcare into account, and a hold-time report at three months.

works_the_facts.reason: The 8-year severance example (16 weeks) makes the offer concrete and the 44%/60% trends are set side by side, but nothing more is drawn from the figures, such as what the 9-minute hold could become.

right_comparison.reason: Doing nothing is described through the trends the facts show (branch visits falling, contacts rising, a 9-minute hold), but it doesn't say where those trends lead if the branches stay open.

qualification.reason: The promise to report hold time at three months gives a date and a number readers can check, but sets no target and no consequence if hold time doesn't improve.

objections.reason: It deals openly with the change in hours and partly with lost member relationships, but it never addresses the core dislike of phone work and ignores the two weeks of rumours, so 'hear this from me first' reads oddly.

fit.reason: It is a COO email of roughly 400 words with a clear subject line and sections, as asked, though it reasonably holds back the 'better for everyone' framing the brief requested.
